pain_points.statement: Finance is 3 weeks behind on invoicing because data does not align across systems, tying up $1.4M in working capital in unbilled receivables.
pain_points.source_excerpt: finance is 3 weeks behind on invoicing because the data never lines up.

pain_points.statement: Stakeholders disagree on the approved budget for Phase 1, with the CFO setting a strict $300k cap while the VP of Operations recalled an approved range of $250k to $400k.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Rita: Marcus, the budget I approved is $300,000. That's the cap. Sarah: Rita, that's not what we discussed. We discussed a six-month Phase 1 in the $250 to $400 range
pain_points.contradiction_note: CFO Rita insists the approved budget cap is $300,000, whereas VP Ops Sarah believed they had agreed on a $250,000 to $400,000 range.

desired_state.statement: Establish a fixed-fee engagement structure with outcome-based milestone payments to manage financial risk.
desired_state.source_excerpt: I'll give you a fixed-fee proposal with milestone payments tied to specific outcomes, and if we miss the milestones you don't pay for them.

success_criteria.statement: Return invoicing cycle time to an industry-standard 5-day DSO, freeing up $1.4M in working capital.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: return to five-day DSO from where we are now frees up about $1.4M in working capital that's currently stuck in unbilled receivables.

success_criteria.statement: Achieve a 30% reduction in dispatch time, avoiding $320k in annual compensation by eliminating the need to hire four additional dispatchers.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: a 30% reduction in dispatch time means we don't need to hire four additional dispatchers next year, which is about $320k in fully-loaded comp.

risks_unknowns.statement: Executive skepticism is high due to a poor vendor experience in 2023 and two failed internal initiatives targeting the same issues.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: I have been burned by this exact conversation before. ... We've tried internal projects to fix this exact thing twice and they both failed.

pain_points.statement: Routemaster suffers from severe technical debt as a 7-year-old custom app, slowing feature delivery by 3x and causing codebase fragility.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Technical debt in Routemaster. We can't ship features anymore because the codebase is too fragile. Every change takes three times as long as it should.

pain_points.statement: High volume of manual data re-entry between the custom Rails dispatch tool and Salesforce CRM.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Too much manual entry between our custom dispatch tool and Salesforce

desired_state.statement: Stakeholders disagree on technical strategy: the CTO favors replacing Routemaster with a $600k/year SaaS platform, while VP Ops favors building an incremental workflow layer on existing infrastructure.
desired_state.source_excerpt: Sarah thinks this is a workflow problem. I think this is a platform problem. Routemaster is seven years old... We can put a band-aid on the dispatcher workflow but in two years we'll be back here
desired_state.contradiction_note: CTO Marcus advocates replacing Routemaster with a full SaaS platform costing $600k in Year 1, whereas VP Ops Sarah wants to solve operational workflow bottlenecks immediately within existing architecture.

success_criteria.statement: Ensure that 60-70% of Phase 1 workflow architecture is portable and reusable if Routemaster is eventually replaced.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: I'd estimate 60-70% of the Phase 1 work survives a platform change.

risks_unknowns.statement: Upcoming federal ELD compliance mandate updates on November 15th require unassessed system integration work.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: The ELD compliance deadline in November is real. The federal mandate update changes how we have to log driver hours and report them.

pain_points.statement: Manual dispatcher data entry creates severe operational friction across 40 dispatchers handling 600 contracted drivers.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Our dispatcher workflow is killing us. Too much manual entry between our custom dispatch tool and Salesforce

pain_points.statement: Drivers dislike the custom React Native mobile app, which has not received major updates since 2023.

desired_state.statement: Focus Phase 1 strictly on invoicing reconciliation and dispatcher workflow automation, deferring driver mobile app changes to Phase 2.
desired_state.source_excerpt: focus on the invoicing reconciliation first... and then the dispatcher workflow... The driver app I'd defer.

success_criteria.statement: Reduce dispatcher manual workload per load by 30%.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: 30% reduction in dispatch time per load

risks_unknowns.statement: Incomplete technology integration following 40% acquisition growth in 2024 poses unknown operational integration obstacles.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: Tech integration from those acquisitions is incomplete.

pain_points.statement: Internal executive disconnect exists between Operations and Technology regarding core problem definition and priority.
pain_points.source_excerpt: Sarah and I have been having a parallel conversation about this for months and we don't agree on what the problem is.

desired_state.statement: Target pilot timeline is disputed: VP Ops and CFO mandate a Q3 (Sept 30) production release to maintain budget allocation, whereas the CTO considers Q4 realistic.
desired_state.source_excerpt: Pilot in production by end of Q3 (Sept 30). / Marcus: Q3 was your commitment, not mine. I never agreed to Q3. I think Q4 is more realistic
desired_state.contradiction_note: CFO Rita and VP Ops Sarah require a production pilot by September 30 (end of Q3) to prevent reallocation of budget funds, while CTO Marcus argues Q4 is the realistic timeframe.

success_criteria.statement: Deploy a pilot to production by September 30 (Q3) to prevent the loss and reallocation of corporate funding.
success_criteria.source_excerpt: If we don't have something in production by end of September, the funding gets reallocated. That part isn't negotiable.

risks_unknowns.statement: Missing the November 15 ELD compliance deadline risks regulatory fines and potential loss of operating authority in certain states.
risks_unknowns.source_excerpt: Fines, possibly losing our operating authority in some states.
